sources.title: Notes on generalized global symmetries in QFT

evidence.text: How do generalized p-form symmetries fit into higher groups, what more general higher-group actions occur in QFT, and can defects, moduli spaces and certain anomalies be interpreted using these structures?

sources.title: On gauging finite subgroups

evidence.text: How do G=Γ/A and the emergent Pontryagin-dual (D−2)-form symmetry Â combine after gauging a non-anomalous finite Abelian normal subgroup A, and how does Γ's anomaly change the answer?

sources.title: Super-higher-form symmetries

evidence.text: How do invertible higher-form symmetries extend to supersymmetric theories, which additional conserved currents arise from supergeometry, and what defects carry their charges?

sources.title: Notes on generalized global symmetries in QFT

evidence.text: Weak associativity is encoded by associator isomorphisms satisfying coherence identities. For finite G, a group-cohomology 3-cocycle with trivial coefficient action supplies the associator and obeys the pentagon identity.

sources.title: On gauging finite subgroups

evidence.text: Domain-wall junctions and Wilson-line phases translate extension data into anomalies. A Γ background decomposes into (a,g) with ∂a=e(g); crossing the junction emits the character phase χ(e(g,h)).

sources.title: Super-higher-form symmetries

evidence.text: Expand currents on supervielbeins, impose differential closure, and integrate them over embedded cycles using distributional Poincaré duals. Exact changes of the dual describe embedding deformations; explicit examples reduce integral-form expressions to ordinary superspace Berezin integrals.

sources.title: Notes on generalized global symmetries in QFT

evidence.text: Homotopy long exact sequences for cosets, gerbe fibrations and higher-group quotients organize proposed defect classifications. Eilenberg-MacLane spaces are used for the preliminary topological classification of extension bundles.

sources.title: Notes on generalized global symmetries in QFT

evidence.text: Loop-space transgression turns gerbes into bundles and higher-group extensions into ordinary central extensions. Bosonization and principal-bundle lifting obstructions supply consistency arguments for the anomaly proposal.

sources.title: On gauging finite subgroups

evidence.text: The LHS spectral sequence has E₂^{p,q}=H^p(G,H^q(A,M)) and converges to H^{p+q}(Γ,M). For trivial Γ action on M, the stated d₂ from the q=1 row is cup product with e. Eilenberg–Mac Lane spaces and Postnikov classes describe mixed-symmetry backgrounds.

sources.title: Fermionic higher-form symmetries

evidence.text: How can invertible fermionic higher-form global symmetries act on extended operators, which tensor-spinor theories realize them, and what obstructs their gauging or preserves/breaks them under interactions and gravitational coupling?

sources.title: Higher-group structure in 2n-dimensional axion-electrodynamics

evidence.text: What higher-group structure is encoded by axion electrodynamics in 2n dimensions, how does it appear in background gauge transformations and anomalies, and what additional operations arise in six dimensions?

sources.title: ICTP lectures on (non-)invertible generalized symmetries

evidence.text: How can generalized internal symmetries be described by topological defects, constructed through gauging, and related to extended charges and the Symmetry TFT?

sources.title: Emergent higher-form symmetry from type IIB superstring theory

evidence.text: Which invertible higher-form global symmetries emerge from gauging the type IIB duality group in its low-energy description, how can their operators measure 7-branes, and how do fermion parity and worldsheet orientation reversal modify them?

sources.title: Mixed anomalies, two-groups, non-invertible symmetries, and 3d superconformal indices

evidence.text: Can the 3d superconformal index detect discrete mixed anomalies and determine which gaugings produce two-group or non-invertible symmetries?

sources.title: Non-invertible global symmetries and completeness of the spectrum

evidence.text: Which properties of gauge-theory defects follow from the gauge group and available dynamical objects, independently of infrared confinement or a gravitational completion?

evidence.text: How do generalized global symmetries and their anomalies constrain QFT dynamics, especially renormalization group flows, confinement, and possible infrared phases?

sources.title: Generalized Global Symmetries

evidence.text: Formulate higher-form global symmetries intrinsically through extended operators, and determine their consequences for selection rules, gauging, duality, spontaneous breaking, anomalies and phases of quantum field theory.

sources.title: Generalised Symmetries in Particle Physics

evidence.text: What do higher-form, higher-group and non-invertible global symmetries teach particle physicists, particularly about axions, unification, dark matter, neutrino masses and flavour?

sources.title: Lectures on generalized symmetries

evidence.text: How are invertible generalized global symmetries defined and computed in QFT, and how do anomalies, gauging, spontaneous breaking and higher-group structures organize gauge-theory physics?

sources.title: On 2-Group Global Symmetries and their Anomalies

evidence.text: How can ordinary and 1-form global symmetries combine into a 2-group, how can its intrinsic data be extracted from symmetry defects, and what are its background couplings and genuine ’t Hooft anomalies?

sources.title: Continuous Generalized Symmetries in Three Dimensions

evidence.text: How can gauging compact scalar couplings with anomalies in parameter space produce continuous 2-group symmetries in three dimensions, and when does the same procedure produce non-invertible defects?

sources.title: Antisymmetric tensor $Z_p$ gauge symmetries in field theory and string theory

evidence.text: How can compact continuous gauge symmetries carried by higher-rank antisymmetric tensors leave discrete Z_p remnants, which extended defects detect them, and how do flux and torsion compactifications realize these sectors?

sources.title: Duality Defect of the Monster CFT

evidence.text: Ising-category F-moves resolve intersections of defect lines. The authors obtain ten torus partition functions with η and N insertions, subject to one linear relation expressing 2A orbifold self-duality.

sources.title: Non-invertible global symmetries and completeness of the spectrum

evidence.text: Test endpoint existence locally: construct a closed linking integral, check its gauge variation on allowed supports, exponentiate, and use its nontrivial linking action in a deformation argument. Every flux and support restriction must remain valid during that deformation.

sources.title: Higher Gauging and Non-invertible Condensation Defects

evidence.text: Insert symmetry-line networks dual to a surface triangulation. Triangulation independence is tested through F-symbols, with pentagon/hexagon consistency relating crossing and braiding. Homology intersection pairings and finite character sums yield fusion and line-action formulas.

sources.title: Non-invertible higher-categorical symmetries

evidence.text: Surface fusion is organized into orbits, followed by generalized gauging on each output surface. Condensation uses an algebra constructed from a junction and its orientation reversal, inserted as a defect mesh; lines after condensation are algebra bimodules.

sources.title: On continuous 2-category symmetries and Yang-Mills theory

evidence.text: Orbit–stabilizer and double-coset decompositions reorganize products of surface orbit sums. The subgroup inclusion Hα∩σHβσ⁻¹⊂H(α+S∨σβ) establishes integrality of the displayed local fusion coefficients.

sources.title: Universal Non-Invertible Symmetries

evidence.text: Compute object fusion by stacking and decomposing vacuum pairs into symmetry orbits. An explicitly imported theorem identifies K₀(2Rep(G)) with a twisted Burnside ring: double cosets determine stabilizer intersections, with restricted and conjugated cocycles supplying the twists.

sources.title: Noninvertible Time-Reversal Symmetry

evidence.text: For p=1, decorate an interface with the three-dimensional action N a∧da/(4π)+a∧dA/(2π). Its equations of motion give a θ jump of −2π/N. General p uses the minimal AN,p TQFT describing Hall filling p/N, composed with naive time reversal.

sources.title: Intermediate defect groups, polarization pairs, and noninvertible duality defects

evidence.text: Quantize the symmetry TFT using a Heisenberg extension of H^k(M,D). Flux operators act as clock and shift operators on a polarization-dependent basis; absolute partition functions are overlaps between the relative partition vector and topological boundary states.

sources.title: Non-invertible symmetries of two-dimensional non-linear sigma models

evidence.text: Introduce a target-space boundary gauge field a to preserve b-field gauge invariance, derive boundary couplings by Noether's method, and track terms surviving half-space integration. Varying the resulting defect action reproduces the on-shell current matching imposed by c|γ=0.

sources.title: Gaillard-Zumino non-invertible symmetries

evidence.text: Construct D_S=U_S×W_S: U_S implements the neutral transformation using the nonconserved current, while W_S interfaces L_S with L. Their fusion restores the same bulk theory on both sides with combined GZ gluing. Topologicity uses stress-tensor invariance imported from the original GZ analysis.

sources.title: Noninvertible Time-Reversal Symmetry

evidence.text: An alternative construction gauges discrete magnetic one-form symmetry in half of spacetime. With pk=1 mod N, combine discrete gauging and counterterm operations with K; the authors use this construction to establish topologicity and conservation and derive condensation-defect fusion.

sources.title: Noninvertible Time-Reversal Symmetry

evidence.text: Analyze background-field transformations and five-dimensional anomaly inflow, then evaluate discrete gauging of quadratic one-form SPT actions. Cup products and Pontryagin squares distinguish odd/even N and bosonic/fermionic cases.
